text: 🇲🇽✊ "There's a part that is a campaign, which is the right, that always rides on anything and makes everything gigantic. But there's another part that is legitimate, from patients and IMSS workers. We cannot say, 'Nothing is happening.'" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 Asked what message the plan sends while complaints about care still circulate online, Sheinbaum said the government listened after a stoppage by some IMSS workers and posts about missing equipment. Staff went floor by floor asking what was needed. Nurses asked for rolling vital-signs monitors: "so you have to buy them." Her example: a knee operation scheduled six months out can now happen in one month, with IMSS's own surgeons operating in extra shifts.

🇲🇽✊ "We reached a salary increase of 8%, similar to last year's, which was 8.1, the highest salary increase there has been in 20 years." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 IMSS director Zoé Robledo presented a 12-action plan for Oct 27 to Feb 24, built from floor-by-floor talks with hospital workers. It includes an 8% raise for 504,000 workers, up from the 6.8% first approved, and permanent posts for 10,939 temporary workers. IMSS will fast-track hiring of 2,500 specialists (the call opens Nov 3) and buy 100 high-tech machines and 2,917 smaller devices. It will add 31,701 surgeries on nights and weekends and stop cancelling specialist appointments in December. Cost: 11.7 billion pesos, funded by buying directly from manufacturers and cutting outsourced services.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Exports Jump 37.9% in September</u>

Mexico exported 77,797 million dollars in September, up 37.9% from a year earlier, INEGI reported. It is the third-highest month on record, behind only July and August of this year. Manufactured exports rose 39% to 72,773 million dollars, and electrical and electronic equipment nearly doubled (+94.7%). Every major export and import category grew, which last happened in January 2023. January-September exports total 627,194 million dollars, up 30.4%.

🇲🇽🇧🇷 <u>Brazilians in Mexico Flip to Lula in the Runoff</u>

At the Brazilian consulate in Mexico City, Brazilians living in Mexico gave Lula 51.51% (699 votes) to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.49% (658). In the first round, Bolsonaro had narrowly led them 45.8% to 45.5%. Ana Marcela da Silva Terra, a public-policy PhD, explained her vote outside the consulate: "for the defense of a country that is sovereign and does not become the backyard of the United States."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Taddei's Resignation Formally Received; Congress Starts Picking Her Successor</u>

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies formally received Guadalupe Taddei's resignation as head of the INE, effective immediately, and sent it to the Political Coordination Board to begin choosing a replacement under Article 41 of the Constitution. With the 2027 elections ahead, Chamber president Raúl Bolaños-Cacho said: "We will be watching from the Chamber of Deputies and we will act at the level that Mexico needs."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Supreme Court Keeps the SAT in the Fight Against Huachicol Fiscal</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously approved four rulings that keep alive the SAT's legal challenges in one of the biggest fuel-smuggling cases on record: more than 21.5 million liters of diesel brought into the country illegally in 2019. The businessmen under investigation tried to get the appeals thrown out by arguing the tax authority had no standing to represent the Treasury. The Court refused to dismiss them.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Launches 12-Action Emergency Plan: 8% Raise, 2,500 Specialists</u>

Mexico's IMSS rolled out a 120-day emergency plan built from what staff told management during hospital visits. It puts 11,745 million pesos into an 8% raise for about 500,000 workers, permanent contracts for 10,939 employees and fast-track hiring of 2,500 medical specialists. The raise starts landing this week, and the plan runs through February 24, 2027.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Mexico Pays 8.3% of Trump's Tariff Take</u>

From January to August, the US collected $14.439 billion in tariffs on imports from Mexico. That is 8.3% of the $173.5 billion Washington raised in tariffs overall, according to US Commerce Department data reported by El Financiero. The bill topped $1.6 billion every month, peaking at $1.977 billion in May and reaching $1.932 billion in August. Mexico is Washington's largest trading partner, yet it pays a small share of the tariffs, because about 85% of its exports still enter duty-free under the T-MEC. Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel, aluminum and copper, and 25% on vehicles, are still charged.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Cota Out Over His Son's Post, Mejía Haro In at Agriculture</u>

Leonel Cota Montaño left Mexico's Agriculture Undersecretariat after his son, Manuel Cota Cárdenas, was named coordinator of the Fourth Transformation defense committees in Baja California Sur, and President Sheinbaum asked for his resignation. A week later, Agriculture Secretary Columba López named his replacement: former Zacatecas mayor and Morena deputy Ulises Mejía Haro. "We add capacity and experience to strengthen national production," López said, "and move toward a fairer, shared countryside."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Who Is Mexican Journalism Working For?</u>

In Contralínea, Ruth Dávila argues that Mexico's commercial press is "permeated by the ideology of the richest 1 percent." She points to what it leaves out: "practically no Mexican media outlet" covers occupied Palestine or the blockade on Cuba. Her proposal, borrowed from Walter Benjamin's "author as producer," is that journalism is "an eminently political exercise," so the job is to "politicize the present, setting sensationalism aside."
